target_customer: Retail and semi-professional traders who have strategy ideas but cannot code
problem: Traders with ideas could not turn them into automated, backtested algorithms without programmers, so strategy building stayed in the hands of coders.
business_model: Freemium trading platform with a planned paid tier for users of other brokers and brokerage economics

founders.name: Soraya Taghavi
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (2017-03) says she worked in trading at Goldman Sachs. The YC page lists her as the only founder and gives no bio.

competitors.name: Quantopian
competitors.what: Free community platform where members write Python trading algorithms, backtest them and can win capital allocations
competitors.traction_then: More than 100,000 community members in Nov 2016
competitors.funding_then: $25M Series C in Nov 2016, about $48.8M to $50M total

technical_complexity.rationale: Parsing English strategy descriptions into rules, running them continuously on market data and backtesting on history is standard engineering with hard natural language parts. The 2017 launch article says users still had to place trades themselves, so no brokerage integration existed yet.

defensibility.rationale: The natural language interface could be copied by brokers or code-based platforms. No data or network effect is described in the sources.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Quantopian shut its retail offering in 2020 per a 2026 directory summary; no source shows an incumbent copying the English interface.

market_need_then: The TechCrunch launch article (2017-03) describes a gap between traders with ideas and the people able to code algorithms. Quantopian's 100,000 member community in 2016 shows demand for algorithm building tools.

branding.domain_note: Uses algoriz.com; no source on how it was obtained.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself was found. A later company named Algorized has a similar spelling, which adds confusion.

outcome_analysis: The YC directory marks Algoriz inactive, but CB Insights still lists it as alive and directories in 2026 describe a working free product, so the cause of any decline is not public and no failure factors are recorded. It raised very little disclosed money, about $120K per one database, and the YC page shows a team of four and a single founder.
notes: Batch conflict: the dataset and YC page say Winter 2016 but TechCrunch (2017-03-03) says Winter 2017, so competition as_of is set to 2017-01. The company site returned HTTP 503, so it is treated as unreachable at research time. The $120K figure rests on a single database (CB Insights) and has no date. Outcome searches found no shutdown report; CB Insights lists it as Seed and Alive, which conflicts with the YC Inactive status. Competitor list limited to one dated source.
